title: Why Romans is difficult
english: This letter to the Romans is thought harder to understand than Paul's other epistles, and I think this happens for two reasons. First, he sometimes uses confused and less explicit expressions. Second, he raises many questions in it, especially questions on which heretics rely when they try to assert that the cause of each person's deeds should be traced not to purpose but to the diversity of nature. Praying to God who teaches man knowledge (Psalm 94:10), we shall take up the beginning of our explanation of Paul's Epistle to the Romans.

title: Paul's service to Christ as adoption, not slavery
english: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ. Let us ask why the man who writes elsewhere, “For you did not receive the spirit of slavery again in fear, but you received the spirit of adoption” (Romans 8:15), calls himself a servant. “Though I am free from all, I made myself a servant to all” (1 Corinthians 9:19). So he serves Christ not in the spirit of slavery but in the spirit of adoption, because Christ's service is nobler than every freedom. Glory to Christ. Amen.
